items.text: on a computer, panels no longer float, pin or drag. Each opens in its own place and closes as before, until a proper desktop system arrives: one pane on the right that holds them all
with a mouse, the caret now shows over ▶ too, saying the scenes and Auto play open above it; a click on the caret opens them, as on the other buttons
at the foot of Auto play, a Scenes in play button with the count beside it (12 of 35); the button opens Scenes, where you tick them in or out
on a slow connection the duck-rabbit could load twice: it landed, then filled up with colour again. It now arrives once, already in colour
Auto play's Every is a row of beads with the count inside; count in seconds, beats or bars, or pick the dice bead for a random length each time. Beats and bars follow the beat that plays
Changes shows the whole scene across the top and its two halves, pattern and style, under it; the whole scene lights both
counts sit at each tile's top right, morph times too; a Pro feature shows a lock, a dotted edge and a faint tint

new words. A scene is the whole thing you save, star and play (it was a look); its pattern is the G-code under it; its style is how the field looks and moves. Looks only is now Built-in, and Random rolls a new style on your pattern
in Auto play, Changes: the whole scene, the style only (your word or pattern stays), or the pattern only (your style stays); ‹ › follow it too
rename a scene of yours with its pencil; editing its pattern has its own icon
Random saves with the same Save this scene button, named for you, no name box
the Random and Scenes lists line up the same way (star, checkbox, row, handle), and a tapped row no longer stays highlighted
leaving the cover, the Beta · version line no longer lingers over the bar as it rises; the bottom row clears first
the arrows that go between panels are slim tabs beside the panel, off its content; touch one and the next panel's icon comes forward, let go to go there
